builds.name: Reference: Ranked jungle core
builds.goal: Reference for Zac: the core and runes ranked Emerald+ jungle players use most (2,763 ranked Emerald+ games with this core on OP.GG, patch 16.20, 49% win rate).
builds.hypothesis: A healing engage tank who enters from terrain, repeatedly disrupts nearby enemies and recovers through collected blobs. The current jungle provider core anchors this plan; later slots are observed options or reviewed kit completions. Core in purchase order: Hextech Rocketbelt → Sunfire Aegis → Spirit Visage. Conqueror keystone as played in those games. Remaining slots: Ionian Boots of Lucidity, Randuin's Omen, Jak'Sho, The Protean.
builds.summary: The proven jungle baseline: Hextech Rocketbelt → Sunfire Aegis → Spirit Visage, with Conqueror.
testPlan: Play it in jungle as your control build. Follow the purchase order; the core (Hextech Rocketbelt → Sunfire Aegis → Spirit Visage) is what ranked players complete first.
Record kills, deaths, damage dealt and the minute you finish each core item, then compare other builds against these numbers in similar games.
Adapt the last two items to the enemy team: armor or magic resist against fed carries, anti-heal against healing, penetration once enemies stack resists.
failureConditions: Your results with this build fall clearly below the 49% ranked baseline over several games in the same role.
The enemy team composition makes the core items poor answers; swap the flexible slots before abandoning the core.
tradeoffs: Proven and predictable, so opponents know what to expect. It is a starting point, not the best build for every matchup.
The observed core and individual options do not establish six-item build statistics. Late slots are kit-based inferences.
Six-slot completion is our kit-based inference, not an observed six-item win-rate build.  Situational options replace an appropriate slot; they are not added as a seventh item.
buyOrder: Core in purchase order: Hextech Rocketbelt → Sunfire Aegis → Spirit Visage.
Boots after the first item unless the lane needs them earlier.
coverageNotes: Source: OP.GG ranked Emerald+ solo/duo, patch 16.20, checked 2026-10-14. Core items and rune page are observed; later slots are observed options or reviewed completions. Win rates describe those games, not a prediction for yours.

Zac gains up to [50]% Move Speed over time and can cast Unstable Matter while bouncing.

Zac's body erupts, dealing [40 / 50 / 60 / 70 / 80] + [(4 / 5 / 6 / 7 / 8 + (0.03) × AP) × (0.01)] max Health magic damage to nearby enemies.

Absorbing Goo reduces this Ability's Cooldown by 1 second.

Zac stretches his arm out, attaching it to the first enemy hit to deal [60 / 90 / 120 / 150 / 180 + (0.3) × AP + (0.03) × Stat(12)[statFormula=2]] magic damage and briefly Slow them. Zac's next Attack gains increased range and applies the same damage and Slow. 

If Zac hits a different enemy with this Attack, he Knocks Up both towards each other. If they collide, they and surrounding enemies take [60 / 90 / 120 / 150 / 180 + (0.3) × AP + (0.03) × Stat(12)[statFormula=2]] magic damage and are briefly Slowed.

Each time Zac hits an enemy with an Ability, he sheds a chunk of Goo that can be reabsorbed to restore [characterLevelInterpolation(0.04 → 0.08; raw flags preserved)] Max Health.

Upon dying, Zac splits into 4 bloblets that attempt to recombine. If any bloblets remain after [characterLevelBreakpoints(start=8, perLevel=0, changes=[{"mLevel": 6, "mAdditionalBonusAtThisLevel": -1.0, "__type": "Breakpoint"}, {"mLevel": 10, "mAdditionalBonusAtThisLevel": -1.0, "__type": "Breakpoint"}, {"mLevel": 13, "mAdditionalBonusAtThisLevel": -1.0, "__type": "Breakpoint"}, {"mLevel": 17, "mAdditionalBonusAtThisLevel": -1.0, "__type": "Breakpoint"}])] seconds, he will revive with 10-50% Health based on the surviving bloblet's Health. This has a [300] second Cooldown.

builds.name: Bounce Goo cooldown
builds.summary: Use R's permitted W casts and Goo pickups to generate additional finite W opportunities.
builds.goal: Use R's permitted W casts and Goo pickups to generate additional finite W opportunities.
builds.hypothesis: R bounces four times and explicitly allows W; W deals AP-scaled max-health magic damage and each absorbed Goo reduces its cooldown by one second. Cosmic and R speed assist pickup paths, Visage increases actual Goo healing and Riftmaker rewards sustained combat. E champion hits spawn extra chunks.
testPlan: Required state: Finite Goo chunks generated by actual hits, pickup path accessible and W cooldown recorded.
Count chunks spawned/absorbed and W casts during one R with versus without pickups, logging health costs.

Run three trials at matched level, ranks, gold and target defenses. Repeat against a moving opponent with a fixed incoming damage pattern. Record damage packets, missed actions, resource cost and survival separately.
Keep souls, health/mana, form, item/rune stacks, transformations and game time finite and explicitly recorded. No free full ramp or infinite scaling.
failureConditions: Enemies deny chunks or the pickup route loses contact with W targets.
The narrow damage gain does not repay lost access, survival, wave control or allied utility.
tradeoffs: Rejected assumption: Four bounces do not prove four full first-hit R packets against one enemy.
Confidence: plausible. Source-compatible reasoning is not in-game validation or proof of novelty/optimality.
buyOrder: Candidate six slots: Riftmaker, Cosmic Drive, Spirit Visage, Liandry's Torment, Abyssal Mask, Ionian Boots of Lucidity. Compare two-item checkpoints before the final six-slot test; this list is not a lane shopping order.
Keep role-appropriate starters, boots and support quest/vision obligations. If the full candidate assumes farmed income, compare it separately from support income.
coverageNotes: Only Cassiopeia Q/E and Sett W have numerical adapters. Even there, these other objectives and item/rune interactions may fall outside the model.
Proc inheritance, crit, pet hits and conditional helpers remain uncertain until observed. No completed mathematical maximum is claimed.

builds.name: Situational adaptation: Magic matchup
builds.goal: Situational adaptation for Zac: adapt to the specified fight rather than assume one universal build
builds.hypothesis: A healing engage tank who enters from terrain, repeatedly disrupts nearby enemies and recovers through collected blobs. Count blobs collected and real knockup/contact time. AP/burn may raise damage but must repay lower defense; blobs out of reach cannot be granted as automatic healing. MR and nearby magic amplification test durable contact against magic pressure.
builds.summary: MR and nearby magic amplification test durable contact against magic pressure.
testPlan: Kit question for Zac: Count blobs collected and real knockup/contact time. AP/burn may raise damage but must repay lower defense; blobs out of reach cannot be granted as automatic healing.

Start with the early core (Hollow Radiance or other MR first when justified) plus appropriate boots at matched gold. Record level, actual ability ranks, forms, resource and item transformations; six-item results do not establish lane strength. Use your intended lane or jungle role; jungle starters and early consumables are outside the final six slots.

Compare against the reference route at the same level, gold spent, finite stacks and opponent setup. Record unused gold; isolate an item change before changing runes. Run three repeatable trials of a short trade and a ten-second fight. Record damage actually landed, attacks/casts, misses, remaining resource and survival. Resource: None. Do not treat mana regeneration as None recovery; Nimbus replaces Manaflow when that Sorcery row is used.

Measure the actual interaction before granting item/rune procs: MR and nearby magic amplification test durable contact against magic pressure. Test once stationary, then with a moving opponent and a fixed incoming damage pattern. Choose the opponent profile this defensive route is intended to address, then repeat against the wrong damage type.

Q evidence: Zac stretches an arm, grabbing an enemy. Attacking a different enemy will cause him to throw both targets towards each other. Keep finite champion/item/rune stacks explicit. Use Practice Tool, a custom match or your own replay; no numerical adapter is available for this champion.
failureConditions: MR is wasted against the wrong threat; nearby aura range and healing eligibility matter.

The route fails Zac's stated kit question: Count blobs collected and real knockup/contact time. AP/burn may raise damage but must repay lower defense; blobs out of reach cannot be granted as automatic healing.
Higher dummy damage is offset by fewer landed actions, deaths before the useful window, or worse ally utility.
tradeoffs: MR is wasted against the wrong threat; nearby aura range and healing eligibility matter.
Full cost 15,600 gold; delayed items, resource starvation and the two-item spike must be judged separately.
Counter-items are conditional. Change boots/defense for the real matchup, then record the modified setup.
buyOrder: Hollow Radiance or other MR first when justified. Adapt component timing to lane/jungle pressure; do not blindly follow the displayed six-item order.
Keep appropriate boots while building the early core; swap boots only when the measured matchup justifies it.
Abyssal Mask, Spirit Visage, Jak'Sho, The Protean are later or conditional slots; do not postpone necessary protection for a six-item ceiling.
Resource: None. Do not treat mana regeneration as None recovery; Nimbus replaces Manaflow when that Sorcery row is used.
coverageNotes: No numerical damage or survival adapter exists for this champion. Loading this proposal opens a manual test sheet, not calculated damage.
Source formulas remain in Champion kit. Symbolic values, unresolved tokens and helper records are evidence to inspect, not a certified executable simulator.
Legal source item/rune references were checked; retained map flags cannot prove every live-shop condition. Confirm shop eligibility, exact on-hit/on-attack rules and real proc cooldowns in game.

builds.name: Stretch attack payoff
builds.summary: Test the Q-granted attack as a delivery window before the two-target collision.
builds.goal: Test the Q-granted attack as a delivery window before the two-target collision.
builds.hypothesis: Q grants the next attack range and its AP/bonus-health damage; attacking a different enemy pulls both together for a collision packet. Dusk rewards the prior Q cast and Nashor supports the attack, while Rocketbelt can adjust the geometry and AP improves E's entry damage.
testPlan: Required state: Q attaches first target, a different target is attackable and Goo costs/pickups recorded.
Log Q first hit, enhanced attack, collision and item packets for same-target versus different-target attacks.

Run three trials at matched level, ranks, gold and target defenses. Repeat against a moving opponent with a fixed incoming damage pattern. Record damage packets, missed actions, resource cost and survival separately.
Keep souls, health/mana, form, item/rune stacks, transformations and game time finite and explicitly recorded. No free full ramp or infinite scaling.
failureConditions: No second target denies collision or the attack range increase still cannot reach it.
The narrow damage gain does not repay lost access, survival, wave control or allied utility.
tradeoffs: Rejected assumption: The Q collision is not established as another on-hit attack copying Dusk/Nashor.
Confidence: speculative. Source-compatible reasoning is not in-game validation or proof of novelty/optimality.
buyOrder: Candidate six slots: Dusk and Dawn, Nashor's Tooth, Hextech Rocketbelt, Riftmaker, Rabadon's Deathcap, Sorcerer's Shoes. Compare two-item checkpoints before the final six-slot test; this list is not a lane shopping order.
Keep role-appropriate starters, boots and support quest/vision obligations. If the full candidate assumes farmed income, compare it separately from support income.
